subject: Re: Hosting confirmation and keystore/VPC boundaries for EU pilot
messages:
From: Beth Adams <beth@starlitehealth.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: security@starlitehealth.com
Date: 2027-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosting geography + keystore boundary questions for pilot

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We're moving the Starlite pilot into our EU environment and need a short packet from Redwood for our security review (SIG/CAIQ + a couple of clarifications). Specifically: 

- Can you confirm which AWS regions and availability zones will host tenant data for the EU pilot (we need explicit region names for our audit team)?
- How is KMS/Vault partitioning handled for private deployments (operator vs tenant keys, backup/escrow flows)?
- Can you share a VPC-level diagram showing private endpoints, peering approach, and any required firewall egress rules?
- Do you have a short excerpt from your SOC 2 that references key management or network controls we can include in the packet?

Target timeline: we'd appreciate the packet by EOD Tuesday (Sep 3) if possible. Attachments OK — PDF or image stubs fine.

Best,
Beth Adams
Senior InfoSec Manager | Starlite Health
Beth@starlitehealth.com

---
Note: we'll need to share this with procurement and our legal team; if there are any required redlines for private peering/keystore escrow let us know now.
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Beth Adams <beth@starlitehealth.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosting geography + keystore boundary questions for pilot

Hi Beth — appreciate the clear list. Short answers and next steps below; sending a compact packet as attachments.

Summary answers:
- Regions: EU pilot nodes will be deployed in eu-west-1 (Ireland) with optional standby nodes in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) if you request multi-zone standby. For your audit, use "eu-west-1 (Ireland)" as primary.
- Keystore: For Redwood Private we support customer-managed KMS (BYOK) or Redwood-managed tenant keys. Operator access to keystores is restricted, logged, and requires dual-approval for export; backups are encrypted and can be delivered to a sealed escrow under NDA.
- VPC/Peering: We'll provide a VPC diagram showing private endpoints, peering vs PrivateLink options, and expected egress CIDR ranges for monitoring/health checks.
- SOC 2 excerpt: Attached is a short SOC 2 excerpt referencing encryption of data at rest and network segmentation controls; full reports available under NDA.

Attachments included: redwood_caiq_answers_v1.pdf, eu-vpc-keystore-diagram.png, soc2-excerpt-2027Q2.pdf

Irene — can you confirm the operator contact and the specific KMS partitioning bullet I should include in the packet? Marissa, FYI on customer ask and potential escrow request.

Beth — happy to hop on a 20-min call tomorrow if you want to walk the packet together.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, EMEA | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
+44 20 7946 0123
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-01T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosting geography + keystore boundary questions for pilot

Markus / Beth — adding operational detail for the packet (short bullets we can paste into CAIQ answers and the diagram caption):

- Region/Node detail: Primary compute and storage for the pilot will be in eu-west-1; logs and audit traces are routed to a dedicated EU logging bucket in eu-west-1. Standby nodes (if requested) are in eu-central-1 and are explicitly documented in the runbook.
- KMS partitioning: Customer-managed KMS (recommended) creates a tenant-specific CMK in your AWS account; Redwood's runtime uses that CMK for envelope encryption only. Redwood-managed keys are stored in our KMS with strict RBAC; operator-facing key material is split (X-of-Y) and never exported without approved escrow.
- Operator access & audit: All operator actions that touch keystore material require ticket + dual-approval, are recorded to an immutable audit log, and retained 2 years for EU customers.
- VPC layout notes: We support two connection patterns — PrivateLink (recommended) or VPC peering. PrivateLink keeps the customer's egress minimal; peering requires explicit route-table entries and security group rules (we'll provide the exact /28 ranges for health and metrics).

Attachments I prepared for the packet: eu-vpc-keystore-diagram.png (annotated), redwood_caiq_answers_v1.pdf (draft), soc2-excerpt-2027Q2.pdf (excerpt).

Marissa — if procurement asks about escrow wording, the standard clause we propose is: "Escrow of sealed key material requires mutual agreement, documented export procedure, and signing of the data-release authorization form." I'll drop the clause in the shared Drive link.

If that's sufficient, Markus — you can send the packet to Beth. If Starlite needs BYOK onboarding steps, I can schedule a short ops call.

Irene Choi
Director, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai
From: Beth Adams <beth@starlitehealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@starlitehealth.com

Markus / Irene — this is exactly what we need, thank you. A couple quick follow-ups: 

- We'll use the eu-west-1 primary designation in our audit.
- Please include the exact /28 egress ranges for PrivateLink health checks in the finalized diagram (we'll need CIDR values to open firewall rules).
- Procurement asks whether you can provide an "escrow readiness" certificate/statement we can attach; otherwise they want to see the exact escrow clause language (NDA ok).

Can you send an updated packet with the CIDR ranges and the escrow clause text by EOD Tuesday (Sep 3)? If so we'll mark this as green from security and route to procurement. If you prefer, we can do a 15-min call to finalize the escrows.

Thanks again,
Beth
